MOCKIT.question: Explain the business, financial trajectory, management guidance delivery, positives and risks.

findings.text: Mock IT Services (MOCKIT) provides recurring services to enterprise customers in India and overseas; management describes repeat customer relationships and better project delivery as strengths. All figures are fictional/synthetic for this exercise.
FY2025 (consolidated, INR crore): revenue 3200, EBITDA 600, PBT 500, PAT 360. FY2026: revenue 3680, EBITDA 660.2, PBT 574, PAT 411 — growth across all four lines year over year.
FY2026 cash from operations was 580 and capital expenditure 100; year-end debt 300 and equity 2000 (INR crore).

Quarterly consolidated revenue (INR crore) rose sequentially across the five reported quarters: 900 (Q2 FY2026, period ended 2025-09-30), 950 (Q3 FY2026), 980 (Q4 FY2026), 1000 (Q1 FY2027), 1200 (Q2 FY2027).

Quarterly EBITDA (INR crore) also rose sequentially: 150, 171, 186.2, 200, 240 over the same five quarters; Q2 FY2027 EBITDA of 240 on revenue of 1200 corresponds to the 20% margin stated in the transcript.
Quarterly PBT/PAT (INR crore): 140/100 (Q2 FY2026), 150/110 (Q3 FY2026), 154/111 (Q4 FY2026), 160/120 (Q1 FY2027), 200/150 (Q2 FY2027) — steady sequential improvement.

Management has repeatedly guided to higher EBITDA margins but has missed each time: guided 20% for FY2026 Q4, delivered 19% (miss by 1.0 pp); guided 21% for FY2027 Q1, delivered 20% (miss by 1.0 pp); guided 22% for FY2027 Q2, delivered 20% (miss by 2.0 pp).

Current outstanding guidance: management explicitly guided for EBITDA margin of 23% in FY2027 Q3 (the quarter following Q2 FY2027). No actual exists yet for that period, so delivery is unverified. No numerical revenue growth guidance or share-price target was provided in any transcript.

Management consistently attributes margin pressure to delayed customer approvals and higher hiring costs, and says project timing remains uncertain when asked about execution risk — the same explanation across the last three quarters.

Revenue, EBITDA, PBT and PAT all grew from FY2025 to FY2026, and quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT have risen sequentially for five straight quarters, indicating an intact growth trajectory despite margin shortfalls.

Cash generation appears healthy relative to investment: FY2026 cash from operations of 580 versus capex of 100, with modest year-end debt of 300 against equity of 2000; repeat client relationships are cited as supporting revenue resilience.

Guidance credibility is a risk: management missed its own EBITDA margin guidance in three consecutive reported quarters, with the miss widening from 1.0 pp (FY2026 Q4, FY2027 Q1) to 2.0 pp (FY2027 Q2), so the outstanding 23% FY2027 Q3 guide may again prove optimistic.

Disclosed risks include delayed customer approvals, hiring costs, and revenue concentration in a few large clients; management also flags uncertain project timing, and the same margin-pressure causes persisting across quarters suggests these are unresolved rather than one-off issues.

INFY.question: Explain the business, financial trajectory, management guidance delivery, positives and risks.

findings.text: Infosys (INFY) provides recurring services to enterprise customers in India and overseas, with management citing repeat customer relationships and better project delivery as strengths. All figures are fictional/synthetic for this exercise.

FY2025 (consolidated, INR crore): revenue 3,200; EBITDA 600; PBT 500; PAT 360. FY2026 (consolidated, INR crore): revenue 3,680; EBITDA 660.2; PBT 574; PAT 411 — growth across all four metrics year over year. FY2026 cash from operations was 580 with capital expenditure of 100; year-end debt was 300 against equity of 2,000.

Quarterly trajectory (consolidated, INR crore): FY2026 Q3 revenue 950 / EBITDA 171 / PBT 150 / PAT 110; FY2026 Q4 revenue 980 / EBITDA 186.2 / PBT 154 / PAT 111; FY2027 Q1 revenue 1,000 / EBITDA 200 / PBT 160 / PAT 120; FY2027 Q2 revenue 1,200 / EBITDA 240 / PBT 200 / PAT 150. Revenue and profit metrics rose sequentially in each of the four reported quarters.

Delivered EBITDA margins per transcripts: FY2026 Q3 18%, FY2026 Q4 19%, FY2027 Q1 20%, FY2027 Q2 20% — a step up from Q3 to Q1 followed by a flat Q2, with management attributing margin pressure in each quarter to delayed customer approvals and higher hiring costs.

Guidance delivery (EBITDA margin, consolidated, per supplied computed comparisons): FY2026 Q4 guided 20% vs actual 19% — missed by 1.0 percentage point; FY2027 Q1 guided 21% vs actual 20% — missed by 1.0 percentage point; FY2027 Q2 guided 22% vs actual 20% — missed by 2.0 percentage points. FY2027 Q3 guided 23% has no actual yet (missing_actual). Management has missed its EBITDA margin guidance in all three quarters where an actual is available, and the shortfall widened in the most recent quarter.

Forward guidance outstanding: management explicitly guided for EBITDA margin of 23% in FY2027 Q3 (quarter following FY2027 Q2). No numerical revenue growth guidance and no share-price target were provided in any transcript.

Guidance vs delivered results distinction: the 23% FY2027 Q3 EBITDA margin figure is forward guidance only, not a delivered result; delivered margins to date are 18% (FY2026 Q3), 19% (FY2026 Q4), 20% (FY2027 Q1) and 20% (FY2027 Q2).

Bull case (evidence-based possibilities): revenue has grown sequentially for four straight quarters (950 → 980 → 1,000 → 1,200 INR crore) with PAT rising from 110 to 150 INR crore, and repeat client relationships are described as supporting revenue resilience; if delayed customer approvals resolve, the guided 23% EBITDA margin for FY2027 Q3 could be achieved, extending the margin recovery from 18% in FY2026 Q3 to 20% in FY2027 Q2.

Bear case (evidence-based possibilities): management has missed its own EBITDA margin guidance three consecutive times (by 1.0, 1.0 and 2.0 percentage points), with the miss widening; the same headwinds — delayed customer approvals and higher hiring costs — have persisted across all four reported quarters, and management itself flags uncertain project timing and execution risk. Revenue concentration in a few large clients adds downside sensitivity if any major client is affected.

CDSL.question: Explain the business, financial trajectory, management guidance delivery, positives and risks.

findings.text: CDSL provides recurring services to enterprise customers in India and overseas; management cites repeat customer relationships and better project delivery as strengths. Revenue is concentrated in a few large clients.

FY2025 (consolidated, INR crore): revenue 3200, EBITDA 600, PBT 500, PAT 360. FY2026: revenue 3680, EBITDA 660.2, PBT 574, PAT 411. FY2026 cash from operations 580, capex 100, year-end debt 300, equity 2000.

Quarterly trajectory (consolidated, INR crore): FY2026 Q3 revenue 950 / EBITDA 171 / PBT 150 / PAT 110; FY2026 Q4 revenue 980 / EBITDA 186.2 / PBT 154 / PAT 111; FY2027 Q1 revenue 1000 / EBITDA 200 / PBT 160 / PAT 120; FY2027 Q2 revenue 1200 / EBITDA 240 / PBT 200 / PAT 150.

Management has missed its own EBITDA-margin guidance for three consecutive quarters: FY2026 Q4 guided 20% vs 19% actual (-1.0 pp, missed); FY2027 Q1 guided 21% vs 20% actual (-1.0 pp, missed); FY2027 Q2 guided 22% vs 20% actual (-2.0 pp, missed). FY2027 Q3 guidance of 23% has no actual yet (missing_actual).
Management explicitly guided FY2027 Q3 EBITDA margin at 23% (forward guidance, not yet delivered). No numerical revenue growth guidance or share-price target was provided in any transcript.

Revenue and profit have grown sequentially every quarter for four quarters (950 -> 980 -> 1000 -> 1200 revenue; PAT 110 -> 111 -> 120 -> 150), and FY2026 revenue, EBITDA, PBT and PAT all exceeded FY2025, with repeat client relationships cited as supporting revenue resilience.
FY2026 cash from operations of 580 crore comfortably exceeded capex of 100 crore, indicating self-funded operations; equity of 2000 crore versus debt of 300 crore at year-end.

Management has missed its EBITDA-margin guidance in each of the last three quarters, with the miss widening to -2.0 pp in FY2027 Q2; margin pressure is attributed to delayed customer approvals and higher hiring costs, and management says project timing remains uncertain.
Disclosed risks include delayed customer approvals, hiring costs, and revenue concentration in a few large clients; execution risk on project timing was flagged in response to an analyst question.
